modules.title: 一次提交怎样产出可识别的发布工件

items.title: 产物把某次源码固定下来
items.text: 构建会结合这次提交、依赖和配置，产出浏览器可加载的文件或可运行镜像。带提交号或版本号的工件让团队知道之后测试和部署的是哪一份内容。

items.title: 成功构建不是用户已经能用
items.text: 构建通过只证明工件被生成；它可能还没部署，也可能部署后测试失败。要继续看环境地址、检查结果和发布状态，不能只看一条绿色构建。

modules.title: 容易混淆的地方
modules.text: 构建不是部署或发布。构建制造工件；部署把工件放入一个环境；发布才让目标用户获得它。三个步骤可以由同一流水线执行，但对应的证据不同。新手最常遇到的构建失败是 TypeScript 类型错误和缺少导入。当终端显示“Type error: Property X does not exist on type Y”时，说明代码试图使用 TypeScript 不认识的属性或函数。把完整的报错信息发给 AI 是最快的解决办法。构建错误会阻断部署——如果构建失败，任何代码都无法到达用户手中。

lessonPractice.title: 流水线显示“Build succeeded”，但测试环境地址还是旧页面。下面哪个判断正确？

options.label: 核对这次构建的版本号，确认测试环境实际部署的是不是同一份工件
options.feedback: 对。构建产物和环境里实际运行的版本不是同一件事。

options.label: 重新执行一次构建，再刷新测试地址，确认旧页面有没有被替换
options.feedback: 重新构建只会再生成工件；如果部署步骤没有使用它，测试环境仍可能保持旧版本。

options.label: 清理浏览器缓存后比较页面变化，把看到新页面作为构建成功的证据
options.feedback: 缓存会影响看到的内容，但页面变化不能证明它对应哪次构建；应核对部署工件或版本标识。

en.title: The pipeline says “Build succeeded,” but the test URL still shows the old page. Which judgment is correct?

options.label: Check this build's version and confirm whether the test environment actually deployed that same artifact
options.feedback: Correct. A build artifact and the version actually running in an environment are different things.

options.label: Run the build again, then refresh the test URL to see whether the old page gets replaced
options.feedback: Building again only produces another artifact. If deployment does not use it, the test environment can remain old.

options.label: Clear browser cache and treat seeing the new page as evidence that this build succeeded
options.feedback: Cache can affect what you see, but a page change does not prove which build it came from. Check the deployed artifact or version identifier.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请为这次提交生成可部署构建产物，并把提交号或版本号写进构建结果。完成后告诉我产物是什么，以及它是否已经部署到测试环境；不要把构建成功当成上线完成。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Generate a deployable build artifact for this commit and include its commit or version identifier in the result. Then tell me what the artifact is and whether it has reached the test environment; do not treat a successful build as release completion.

learning.assumes: You know source code must pass through a command or pipeline before others can run it.
learning.outcome: You can distinguish an identifiable build artifact from whether it has been deployed, verified, or opened to users.

modules.title: How one commit produces an identifiable release artifact

items.title: An artifact fixes one source version
items.text: A build combines the commit, dependencies, and configuration into browser-loadable files or an image. A commit or version identifier tells the team what testing and deployment are using.

items.title: A successful build is not usable product evidence
items.text: It only proves an artifact was generated; it may not be deployed or may fail after deployment. Check the environment URL, test results, and release state separately.

modules.title: What it is not
modules.text: Build is not deployment or release. Build makes an artifact; deployment places it in an environment; release makes it available to target users. One pipeline can perform all three, but each needs different evidence. The most common build failures beginners encounter are TypeScript type errors and missing imports. When the terminal shows 'Type error: Property X does not exist on type Y', it means the code tries to use a property or function that TypeScript doesn't know about. Sending the exact error message to AI is the fastest fix. Build errors block deployment - if build fails, nothing reaches the users.

distinctions.label: Deployment
distinctions.text: {c:build} turns source into a runnable or releasable artifact. {c:deployment} places a selected artifact into a target environment for intended users or systems.
